feedback.problem:
From **left to right**, the vertical asymptotes of $f(x)=\frac{1}{x-3}-\frac{1}{x+7}$ are

$x=$
{{field-1}} 
$\,$ and $\,x=$
{{field-2}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's put the two terms over a common denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{x-3}-\frac{1}{x+7} & =\frac{x+7-(x-3)}{(x-3)(x+7)} \\  & =\frac{10}{(x-3)(x+7)}\end{aligned}
$$

There are no common factors in the numerator and denominator, so we proceed to set the denominator equal to zero and get

$$
(x-3)(x+7)=0\,⟹\,x=-7\,,\,x=3.
$$

Therefore, from left to right, the vertical asymptotes are at $x=-7$ and $x=3.$
